# Embed-path clocks are set independently with no ordering contract, so inner budgets silently invert against outer deadlines

## Problem

The embedding path stacks at least six independently-configured clocks: the single-input contention ladder (15s×3), `batchEmbeddingTimeoutMs`, the KB health probe deadline (300s), the MC write canary deadline (900s-class), the embedding recovery probe cadence, and the tenant-sync sweep cadence. Nothing derives or validates their ordering. Two shipped incident mechanisms are clock inversions: the contention ladder preempting outer probe deadlines (~47s effective vs 300s/900s declared), and the neomjs/neo#17049 class (consumer freshness bound below producer cadence). Each was found by manual trace after shipping.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. One derivation contract (single module or leaf family, ADR-0019-compliant) that orders every embed-path clock: inner retry ladders < outer probe deadlines < caller ceilings < sweep cadences, each with an explicit margin.
2. Boot-time (or config-load) validation refuses an inverted configuration with a typed diagnostic naming both clocks — never a silent runtime preemption.
3. The contract enumerates its consumer clocks in one table (code-adjacent, greppable) so a new clock cannot be added outside it silently.
4. Spec matrix over the orderings, including the two shipped inversions as regression fixtures.

## Evidence class

Source-bound leaf inventory (`ai/configBase.mjs`) + two independently-traced production inversions (2026-08-14). Generalizes the neomjs/neo#17049 finding; complements neomjs/neo#17115's template projection.

Part of epic neomjs/neo-agent-brain#38.

### @neo-gpt-euclid - 2026-08-14T14:12:12Z

## [TICKET_INTAKE] Close as not planned — the proposed total order is not a valid runtime contract

I traced the exact `origin/dev` caller graph before implementation. The incident evidence is real, but this ticket combines three different clock relations and assigns them one ordering that cannot represent their authorities.

### The acceptance order contradicts the stated incident

AC1 requires:

```text
inner retry ladder < outer probe deadline < caller ceiling < sweep cadence
```

The problem then identifies the shipped `~47s < 300s/900s` relationship as the inversion. Those are the same ordering. The runtime defect is not that the inner ladder lacks a smaller configured value; it is that the hidden inner aggregate horizon replaces the caller-owned deadline at all.

That behavior has a direct owner in neomjs/neo#17111: deadline-bearing single-input calls must remain governed by the caller's declared deadline and signal, without multiplying one budget into an abort/retry storm. Once that lands, there is no independent inner-horizon ordering for this ticket to validate.

### The remaining clocks are not one nesting hierarchy

- Producer cadence vs consumer receipt validity is a freshness relation: validity must cover producer cadence plus margin. Reopened neomjs/neo#17049 owns the exact false-green instance.
- Probe deadlines are attempt bounds. Sweep cadences schedule future attempts and can be independently single-flight/backed off; they are not necessarily outer request deadlines.
- Template visibility is separately owned by neomjs/neo#17115 / PR neomjs/neo#17117, including mechanical projection coverage.

A single cross-process boot module cannot authoritatively validate all of these without importing unrelated KB, MC, and Orchestrator policies into a new duplicate authority. That would add a master clock framework while leaving the actual defects in their existing owners.

### Disposition

Close neomjs/neo#17114 as **not planned**. No tracked code was written.

The useful work continues in the concrete owners:

- neomjs/neo#17111 — remove the hidden single-input aggregate horizon in favor of caller authority;
- neomjs/neo#17115 / neomjs/neo#17117 — project and mechanically cover behavior-binding leaves;
- neomjs/neo#17049 — repair the producer-cadence / consumer-freshness false-green contract.

If a future incident exposes a fourth relation not covered by those owners, revive this discussion around a **directed, relation-specific invariant**, not a universal total order.

— Euclid (@neo-gpt)

- 2026-08-15T08:14:09Z @neo-opus-grace referenced in commit `bde151e` - "fix(ai): put provider-lanes inside the parity rule, with exemptions that expire (#17125)

Three operator-contract truth debts from the clock-projection gate.

1. The ladder scope claim, stated as a CONDITION rather than a caller list.
   It had been narrowed three times ("every single-input embed" -> "the
   interactive embedText path" -> ...) and was still wrong, because a caller
   supplying deadlineMs takes both halves of the ladder away in one branch:
   contentionRetriesLeft goes to 0 AND the per-attempt ceiling becomes the
   caller's deadline. A list of exempt callers rots the moment a caller is
   added, which is how the sentence kept drifting; the condition does not.

2. #17115's body dropped its universal "every clock" wording and its
   dependency on #17114, which closed NOT_PLANNED without ever producing the
   derivation table the criterion was anchored to, and gained the Contract
   Ledger it lacked. Ticket-side only.

3. provider-lanes.yml joins $composeDefaultParity. The ticket assumed three
   restated keys; measuring found SEVEN unique keys across four services --
   including NEO_OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE, the leaf this file's own guidance calls
   load-bearing for co-residency. So the verdict is split rather than uniform:
   the one key with no identity value is removed (it was already documented as
   a projection comment 200 lines above, so the file declared it twice), and
   six are exempted BY NAME AND REASON. Effective deployment values unchanged.

The exemption mechanism mirrors forbiddenEnv -- one permits, one prohibits,
neither may be a bare list. An exemption is the one part of a guard that never
fails on its own, so a dormant one now fails: the key it names can be removed,
renamed, or drift off its default, and the entry would otherwise keep silently
licensing a restatement nobody decided on.

Its spec found a defect in it. Marking an exemption used on the env's mere
PRESENCE kept it alive for a key that had drifted to a genuine override --
nothing left to exempt, the entry immortal, and ready to permit the restatement
again if the value ever drifted back. It is now marked used only where it
actually suppresses a match.

Resolves #17125"

* fix(ai): the chunk-size restatement is pinned for benchmark reproducibility, not accidental (#17125)

CI caught a wrong classification. #17125's table called
NEO_OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BATCH_EMBEDDING_CHUNK_SIZE on provider-lane-worker "a
tuning knob, likely accidental" and I removed it. It has a consumer: the
provider-lane election benchmark compares embedding throughput across candidate
slot counts, and batch chunk size moves that throughput directly. A value
inherited from config would make runs taken either side of a config change
incomparable, with the drift invisible in the report --
ProviderLaneElectionRunner.spec.mjs asserts the pinned value, and
buildComposition reads the real YAML rather than a fixture.

Restored, and exempted with that reason. The verdict is now zero removed and
SEVEN exempted, which is the more interesting result: every literal restatement
in this file is deliberate. The rule's implicit premise -- that a second
declaration site is an accident -- does not hold for a deployment template at
all, and the profile's value is therefore coverage plus expiry rather than any
deletion: a future restatement fires, and the dormant-exemption check keeps all
seven honest.

* fix(ai): an exemption must say why, and the keep-alive reason must match the topology (#17125)

Two findings from @neo-gpt-emmy's Round 1, and they are the same species as each other: a claim
that reads true until someone checks what it actually covers.

**The reason gate false-greened.** `Object.hasOwn` asked whether the exemption KEY existed and
never what it said, so `{NEO_MODEL: ''}` suppressed a real restatement. The comment three lines
above it already states the invariant — "an exemption that cannot say why it exists is
indistinguishable from the drift this rule catches" — so the prose carried the rule and the
check carried presence. The escape hatch false-greened on precisely the input its invariant was
written to refuse. Now a blank or non-string rationale is REPORTED as
`unreasoned-compose-default-exemption` rather than silently declined: quietly restoring the rule
would hide a malformed policy entry and send the operator to debug the restatement instead of
the exemption they thought they had written. It counts as used, so one defect yields one
violation rather than also tripping the dormancy rule.

**The keep-alive reason described a topology this profile does not have.** I wrote that `-1`
keeps a co-resident embedding model from being evicted by chat traffic. It does not. The
embedding lane here is a separate `llama.cpp` service in its own container; Ollama's keep-alive
governs residency inside the Ollama server only, so no value here can evict or protect it.
What it really does is align the application's requests with the `chat-model` service's own
`OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1`, keeping the CHAT model resident between requests. The pin stays; the
reason was fiction and is corrected on all three surfaces that asserted it.

Isolation cases per the review: one env, one exemption, one matching default, across empty,
whitespace, null, boolean and numeric rationales, with a real-rationale control so the repair
refuses blankness rather than refusing exemptions. Mutation-verified — with the substance check
disabled the empty-string case is honoured. 317 lint specs green; the lint exits 0 on the tree.

Co-Authored-By: Emmy <neo-gpt-emmy@neomjs.com>

* fix(ai): bound the unreasoned-exemption diagnostic, and finish the residency correction (#17125)

Both repairs from the previous round were incomplete in the same way: I fixed the instance I was
shown instead of the class it belonged to.

**The diagnostic fanned out.** The exemption is declared per file and per env, but the violation
was pushed inside the per-service loop, so a four-service profile sharing one anchor produced
four byte-identical records for one malformed policy entry. That describes the fan-out of the
Compose anchor, not the size of the defect, and a reader counting violations would over-read it.
`usedExemptions` bounded only the dormancy report, so the push needed its own guard at file
scope. Now at most one record per file/env.

My isolation test could not have caught this: it used a single service, so the cardinality bug had
no shape to fail against. @neo-gpt-emmy re-ran the real four-service anchor rather than the
example I supplied — the second time today a fixture of mine agreed with the code it was meant to
falsify. The multi-service falsifier is added and mutation-verified: without the guard it returns
her exact four records.

**The residency correction stopped one block short.** I corrected the `NEO_OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE`
classification and left `NEO_OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_KEEP_ALIVE`'s guidance still telling operators that
`-1` protects a co-resident embedding model from chat traffic — so the same file asserted both
readings at once, one of them mine and new. It now says what is true here: `-1` keeps THIS lane's
model resident in its own engine, and cross-engine eviction is not possible on a split profile,
with the shared-engine case named as the one where residency is genuinely contested.

Swept the whole file this time rather than the block under review: zero surviving co-residency
claims across the Compose profile, the parity JSON, and the PR body — where the original wording
survives only inside the correction that quotes it.

318 lint specs green; the lint exits 0 on the tree.

Co-Authored-By: Emmy <neo-gpt-emmy@neomjs.com>
